newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-BAYERN, LEVERKUSEN HEAD TOWARDS TENSE FINALE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BAYERN, LEVERKUSEN HEAD TOWARDS TENSE FINALE.

text.p: Bayer Leverkusen kept up the pressure on Bayern Munich in the tight run-in to the German league title race with a 3-0 victory over struggling St Pauli on Saturday.

Second-half goals from German international striker Ulf Kirsten, Dutchman Erik Meijer and midfielder Hans-Peter Lehnhoff helped Leverkusen narrow the gap on Bayern to just one point with two games remaining.
Bayern took a brief four-point lead with a 3-0 victory at Hansa Rostock on Friday.
The Bavarians have a tougher last two games than their rivals, starting with a top-of-the-table clash with VfB Stuttgart in Munich next weekend.
Leverkusen, who just avoided relegation last season, are chasing their first-ever championship although they have triumphed on the European stage, winning the UEFA Cup in 1988.
After Saturday's victory they are almost certain to get one of the two qualifying places from Germany for next season's lucrative European Cup.
Reigning champions and European Cup finalists Borussia Dortmund, who beat Werder Bremen 2-1 at home on Saturday, are now six points behind Leverkusen in third place.
Leverkusen need only one point to stop Dortmund qualifying for the Champions League. Borussia would then have to win this month's European Cup final to qualify.
Fourth-placed Stuttgart lost vital ground when they were beaten 2-0 at home by Duisburg.
The day was also disappointing for Schalke, who lost 2-1 at 1860 Munich ahead of next week's second leg of the UEFA Cup final with Internazionale Milan.
Leverkusen's victory ended St Pauli's already slim hopes of avoiding the drop into the second division and kept Kirsten firmly on top of the Bundesliga scorers' list with 22 goals.
The home side had struggled to break down St Pauli's defence until the former East German hit the 100th Bundesliga goal of his career in his 200th league match.
But team coach Christoph Daum said he had been confident of victory and was looking forward to next week's local derby at Cologne.
"St Pauli battled hard but I knew we would score," he said. "Now I'm looking forward to the next match. We are going to see a great finale to the season."

On Friday Juergen Klinsmann showed his determination to help Bayern clinch the title despite his imminent departure to Sampdoria with a superb goal against Rostock before explaining why he had decided to play in Italy rather than England next season.

Just a few hours after Sampdoria announced that the German captain was joining them next season, Klinsmann effectively sealed the three points for Bayern when he struck the second goal in the 56th minute.
It was a brilliant effort as he controlled a pass superbly with his head, sprinted to the right side of the box and fired the ball inside the far post.

Klinsmann, who has been frustrated by Bayern's defensive tactics this season, said he had turned down better offers because Sampdoria were an attacking team and his family would feel at home in Italy.

"I had more lucrative offers, especially from England," said Klinsmann, who played in Italy with Inter Milan in the late 1980s. "But Sampdoria are a really attacking team. I also want to go where I can feel the best (in my private life)."
Klinsmann, who recently became a father for the first time, has a house at Como near Milan and is known to enjoy the Italian way of life.
